title: Weak randomized recognition from randomized recognition
statement: Let $E$ be a verifier model, let $L$ be a language of bit strings, and let $c$ be a natural number. If some verifier runs efficiently, accepts every member of $L$ with probability at least $2/3$ using a polynomial number of random bits, and rejects every nonmember for every choice of those bits, then there is an efficient verifier with a polynomial random-bit bound that accepts each member $x$ with probability at least $\min\{2/3,(|x|+1)^{-c}\}$ and still rejects every nonmember for every choice of its random bits.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language of bit strings
$L$ has an efficient verifier with polynomially many random bits, acceptance probability at least $2/3$ on members, and certain rejection on nonmembers
